key_idea: For a segment size s there are s offsets and each needs about n/s segment sums, so one size costs O(n) with prefix sums; iterating over the at most 1001 sizes is fast enough.
sketch: Compute prefix sums. For every size s in [l,h] and every first-segment length o in 1..s, walk the boundaries o, o+s, ... (clamped to n) and count segments with positive sum, tracking the global min and max. Total work is about n * (h-l+1) * (1 + small) = 3e7. Pitfalls: partial segments at both ends are counted, 'profitable' is strictly positive, and o = s (no partial head) must be included. Checked against a brute force on random small inputs.
